text:
ConocoPhillips fell modestly today as oil prices declined—US crude dropped to $96.41 a barrel, down from recent highs as Saudi Arabia restored significant pipeline flows through the Red Sea and Iran ramped exports back toward war-time peaks. When crude supply improves and prices weaken, oil producers like ConocoPhillips face lower revenue per barrel, which typically pressures their stock. The decline extends a two-week slide of nearly 11%, suggesting investors have been repricing the stock downward as geopolitical tensions that had tightened global supply have begun to ease.

The broader backdrop adds complexity: while near-term oil prices are under pressure from recovering exports, Shell's commitment to a $23 billion LNG expansion in Canada and ongoing U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks both signal longer-term energy security concerns that could eventually support prices. However, those longer-dated supports haven't yet offset the immediate headwind of crude flowing back into markets.
